questions.question: Which line divides the Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres?
questions.explanation: The Equator divides the Earth into two hemispheres.

questions.question: The concept of "Directive Principles of State Policy" was borrowed from which country?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

questions.question: The Sundarbans delta is formed by which rivers?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans is formed by the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta.

questions.question: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India established?
questions.explanation: The RBI was established in 1935.

questions.question: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the:
questions.explanation: The Vice-President chairs the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: The RBI is headquartered in Mumbai.

questions.question: The chemical symbol for gold is:
questions.explanation: Gold’s symbol Au comes from Latin "aurum".

questions.question: Which schedule of the Constitution deals with anti-defection?
questions.explanation: The 10th Schedule contains the anti-defection provisions.

questions.question: Which disease is caused by a deficiency of iodine?
questions.explanation: Iodine deficiency causes goitre.

questions.question: Which is the southernmost point of mainland India?
questions.explanation: Kanyakumari is the southernmost point of mainland India (Indira Point is the southernmost of Indian territory).

questions.question: Which organ in the human body purifies blood?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter and purify blood.

questions.question: Which amendment is known as the "Mini Constitution"?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is called the "Mini Constitution" for its sweeping changes.

questions.question: The national flower of India is the:
questions.explanation: The lotus is India’s national flower.

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has 4 chambers.

questions.question: Which acid is present in the human stomach?
questions.explanation: The stomach uses hydrochloric acid for digestion.

questions.question: Photosynthesis mainly takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll where photosynthesis occurs.

questions.question: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Gandhi in:
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920.

questions.question: Which festival is known as the "Festival of Lights"?
questions.explanation: Diwali is the Festival of Lights.

questions.question: The "Right to Education" was made a fundamental right by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A — Right to Education.

questions.question: The national song of India is:
questions.explanation: "Vande Mataram" is the national song; "Jana Gana Mana" is the national anthem.

questions.question: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium and cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.question: The Western Ghats run parallel to which coast of India?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats run along the western coast.

questions.question: Mount Everest is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest lies on the Nepal–China border, with its peak in Nepal.

questions.question: The study of living organisms is called:
questions.explanation: Biology is the study of life and living organisms.

questions.question: The unit of electrical resistance is the:
questions.explanation: Electrical resistance is measured in ohms.

questions.question: The headquarters of the United Nations is in:
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters is in New York City.

questions.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.explanation: Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir is the largest freshwater lake in India.

questions.question: Which day is celebrated as International Yoga Day?
questions.explanation: International Yoga Day is 21 June.

questions.question: The Simon Commission came to India in:
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission arrived in 1928 and was widely boycotted.

questions.question: The powerhouse of the cell is the:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce energy (ATP), so they are the cell’s powerhouse.

questions.question: The "Gateway of India" is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Gateway of India is in Mumbai.

questions.question: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver is the largest gland in the human body.

questions.question: Who gave the slogan "Do or Die"?
questions.explanation: Gandhi gave "Do or Die" during the Quit India Movement.

questions.question: Who founded the Arya Samaj?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875.

questions.question: The Ranji Trophy is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Ranji Trophy is a domestic first-class cricket competition.

questions.question: Who decides the repo rate in India?
questions.explanation: The RBI sets the repo rate through its Monetary Policy Committee.

questions.question: Who composed the song "Vande Mataram"?
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote "Vande Mataram".

questions.question: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and:
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in 1526, founding the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: The SI unit of electric current is the:
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes.

questions.question: The process by which plants lose water through leaves is called:
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves.

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain peak entirely within India?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi is the highest peak entirely within India.

questions.question: The minimum age to become the President of India is:
questions.explanation: A presidential candidate must be at least 35 years old.

questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O-negative is the universal donor blood group.

questions.question: Which is the densest planet in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Earth is the densest planet in the solar system.

questions.question: The Nobel Prize is NOT awarded in which field?
questions.explanation: There is no Nobel Prize in Mathematics.

questions.question: The Param Vir Chakra is awarded for:
questions.explanation: The Param Vir Chakra is India’s highest wartime gallantry award.

questions.question: How many players are there in a cricket team on the field?
questions.explanation: A cricket team fields 11 players.

questions.question: The Rajya Sabha has a maximum strength of:
questions.explanation: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: The INC was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
questions.explanation: Article 32 is called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution.

questions.question: What is 15% of 300?
Find the simple interest on ₹1600 at 5% per annum for 5 years.
Find the compound interest on ₹4000 at 5% per annum for 2 years.
An article costing ₹1000 is sold for ₹1100. Find the profit percentage.
An article costing ₹640 is sold at a 10% profit. Find the selling price.
Find the average of the first five multiples of 2.
questions.explanation: Multiples: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Sum = 30. Average = 30/5 = 6.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 7 and their sum is 40. Find the larger number.
questions.explanation: Total parts = 10. Each part = 40/10 = 4. Larger = 7 × 4 = 28.

questions.question: A train 200 m long crosses a pole in 10 seconds. Find its speed in km/h.
A can do a work in 10 days and B in 40 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.explanation: Combined one-day work = 1/10 + 1/40 = 50/400. Time = 400/50 = 8 days.

questions.question: Find the area of a circle with radius 14 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Area = πr² = (22/7) × 14² = 616 cm².

questions.question: Find the value of √225.
After a 10% discount, an item costs ₹630. Find its marked price.
Find 50% of 10% of 300.
Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7 and their difference is 18. Find the smaller number.
questions.explanation: Difference = 2 parts = 18, so each part = 9. Smaller = 5 × 9 = 45.

questions.question: A boat travels 72 km downstream in 4 hours. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/h, find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 72/4 = 18 km/h = boat + stream. Boat = 18 − 3 = 15 km/h.

questions.question: Find the value of ∛5832.
A train 180 m long crosses a platform 120 m long in 15 seconds. Find its speed in km/h.
questions.explanation: Total distance = 180 + 120 = 300 m in 15 s = 20 m/s = 72 km/h.

questions.question: What is 20% of 580?
Find the simple interest on ₹1900 at 4% per annum for 4 years.
Find the compound interest on ₹5000 at 10% per annum for 2 years.
An article costing ₹600 is sold for ₹690. Find the profit percentage.
An article costing ₹400 is sold at a 5% profit. Find the selling price.
Find the average of the first five multiples of 9.
Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 and their sum is 49. Find the larger number.
questions.explanation: Total parts = 7. Each part = 49/7 = 7. Larger = 4 × 7 = 28.

questions.question: A can do a work in 12 days and B in 6 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.explanation: Combined one-day work = 1/12 + 1/6 = 18/72. Time = 72/18 = 4 days.

questions.question: If today is Sunday, what day will it be after 17 days?
questions.explanation: 17 mod 7 = 3; Sunday + 3 = Wednesday.

questions.question: Which letter is 2nd to the right of the 14th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: 14th letter = N; 14 + 2 = 16th letter = P.

questions.question: Find the odd pair: (5, 125), (6, 216), (9, 729), (2, 10)
questions.explanation: In each correct pair the second number is the cube of the first. 2³ = 8, not 10.

questions.question: In a row of 59 students, Ravi is 12th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 59 − 12 + 1 = 48.

questions.question: Find the next term: 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, ?
questions.explanation: These are perfect squares 7²…11². Next is 12² = 144.

questions.question: Find the next term: 4, 9, 17, 28, 42, ?
questions.explanation: Differences increase by 3 each step; next difference is 17, so 42 + 17 = 59.

questions.question: If BOOK is coded as CPPL, how is SUN coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 1. Applying the same to SUN gives TVO.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 1:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark = 30°. At 1:00 the angle is 1 × 30° = 30°.
The relation is squaring: 5² = 25, so 6² = 36.

questions.question: A person walks 3 km East and then 4 km North. What is the shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km.

questions.question: If + means ×, and × means −, then evaluate: 6 + 3 × 5.
questions.explanation: Replace symbols: 6 × 3 − 5 = 18 − 5 = 13.

questions.question: Find the next term: 2, 6, 18, 54, ?
questions.explanation: Each term follows ×3: 54 × 3 = 162.

questions.question: Complete the series: H, J, L, N, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter advances by 2 places, so the next is P.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 17, 23, 16, 31
questions.explanation: 31, 17, 23 are prime numbers; 16 is a composite number.

questions.question: Which letter is 5th from the right end of the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: The 5th letter from the right is the 22nd from the left = V.
The relation is cubing: 4³ = 64, so 7³ = 343.

questions.question: If today is Tuesday, what day will it be after 59 days?
questions.explanation: 59 mod 7 = 3; Tuesday + 3 = Friday.

questions.question: Which letter is 7th to the right of the 8th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: 8th letter = H; 8 + 7 = 15th letter = O.

questions.question: Find the odd pair: (4, 64), (3, 27), (2, 8), (5, 123)
questions.explanation: In each correct pair the second number is the cube of the first. 5³ = 125, not 123.

questions.question: In a row of 29 students, Ravi is 12th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.explanation: Position from right = 29 − 12 + 1 = 18.

questions.question: Find the next term: 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, ?
questions.explanation: These are perfect squares 6²…10². Next is 11² = 121.

questions.question: Find the next term: 5, 7, 11, 17, 25, ?
questions.explanation: Differences increase by 2 each step; next difference is 10, so 25 + 10 = 35.

questions.question: If DOG is coded as GRJ, how is FISH coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 3. Applying the same to FISH gives ILVK.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 2:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark = 30°. At 2:00 the angle is 2 × 30° = 60°.
The relation is squaring: 8² = 64, so 11² = 121.
